relations.subject: n1ql:drop-user
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - captures a cascading side-effect (deleting the user implicitly revokes every role/privilege it held), distinct from the explicit, user-initiated revocation modeled by the REVOKE statement. Same target shape as `grantsRole`/`revokesRole` minted for GRANT/REVOKE, so it is reused across this batch rather than minting a separate 'cascade revoke' predicate.
relations.evidence: It removes the user from all groups and revokes all roles and privileges assigned to that user.

cross_product_finding: Same management-plane/data-plane split as CREATE BUCKET/CREATE USER. This page also confirms the cascading nature of user deletion in the RBAC role model: dropping a user is not just a management-plane act but has data-plane consequences (group membership and role/privilege revocation), evidenced directly in text rather than inferred. The statement's own framing - 'the Couchbase Server Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system' - again uses 'Couchbase Server', reinforcing the createuser.json finding that the underlying RBAC model is shared with server/, and only the management-plane gate is Capella-specific.
